The statement that the patient "denies any history of sojourning at high altitudes" does not state its reference point relative to the 4,800-m ascent described earlier in the same case.
Past medical history is called unremarkable without naming conditions.

attribution_limitations: Figure 5 Doppler readout shows a peak velocity of about 350 cm/s and a gradient of about 49 mmHg in pixels, whereas the case text gives a peak regurgitant velocity of 4.3 m/s; the article does not say the printed readout is the same measurement.

The abstract says chest CT confirmed right heart enlargement and main pulmonary artery dilation after sentences about both cases; it does not say which case the CT sentence covers, and the case text reports cardiomegaly and a measurement without the word dilation.

The exclusion statements for left heart disease and lung disease (no echocardiographic evidence, chest CT without emphysema, interstitial lung disease or masses) sit under the Case 2 heading but are unlabeled; only the CTEPH line uses the plural "Patients".
The estimated sPAP is stated as exceeding 55 mmHg in both patients, while the case text gives approximately 56 mmHg for this patient.

The discussion says Case 2 showed no significant reduction in sPAP, while the printed estimated sPAP values are approximately 56 mmHg at presentation and approximately 47 mmHg at follow-up; the article does not define "significant".
The statement that the patient "denies any history of sojourning at high altitudes" does not state its reference point relative to the 4,300-m ascent described earlier in the same case.

The discussion lists secondary polycythemia, decompensation and rapid progression among features of "our cases" without naming a case or giving a patient-level polycythemia finding; hemoglobin is 180 g/L in the case laboratory text.
The limitation sentence about right heart catheterization is incomplete in the source, so it does not state whether catheterization was performed.
The time of the amaurosis episode ("One week prior") and the re-ascent ("10 days before presentation") share an implied reference point (presentation) that the amaurosis sentence does not name.
